task_name: The live terminal on the page

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and the diff produces all three. 'Renders as a real terminal': `@xterm/xterm@^6.0.0` joins `dependencies`, `SessionTerminal.tsx:28-29` builds `new Terminal({ cols: COLUMNS, rows: ROWS })` and opens it on the ref'd `.session-terminal__screen`, and `css/xterm.css` is imported so the emulator has its stylesheet. 'Shows what it prints': `onBytes: (bytes) => terminal.write(bytes)` (line 33), which also carries the first scrollback frame the backend sends. 'Takes what is typed': `terminal.onData((text) => void SessionsClient.type(session.id, text))` (line 30), asserted against the literal POST body. 'Names what went wrong': `onRefused` renders `Esta sesión ya no existe` and `onFailure`/`onUnreachable` render `No se puede leer esta sesión`, both through the design system's `Banner type="error" role="alert"`, inside a `<section aria-label="Terminal de la sesión">`. On-screen behaviour holds up: the tokens the CSS reads (`--background-inverse`, `--foreground-inverse`, `--border-subtle`, `--shape-container-sm`) all resolve in `src/system-ui/theme/tokens/`, and the banner's title text is a direct text child of `banner__title`, which is why the copy assertions find it. One thing the objective does not reach: a keystroke whose POST fails is not named on screen (`void SessionsClient.type(...)` discards a rejected promise), but that call is prescribed verbatim by the Contract block, and the brief's failure taxonomy is the stream's, not the input's — so it is the plan's line, not a gap of this diff.

The `**TDD:**` line asks for `it('the bytes the stream delivers are written to the terminal')` — with `@xterm/xterm` doubled, a frame of `hola` leaves `hola` in the fake terminal. `SessionTerminal.test.tsx:54-60` is that test, with that name: it renders, delivers `FakeEventSource.last().receive('{"bytes":"hola"}')` and asserts `expect(lastTerminal().written).toEqual(['hola'])`. Same assertion, same input, same expected value. The assertion is on what the production `onBytes` callback handed the emulator, so it dies if `terminal.write(bytes)` is removed — which the implementer declared it mutated by hand.

Name by name against the Contract block. `export type SessionTerminalProps = { session: LiveSession }` and `export const SessionTerminal = ({ session }: SessionTerminalProps): ReactElement` match exactly. One `useEffect` keyed on `[session.id]`; 80 columns and 24 rows; `terminal.open(screen)` on the ref'd `<div className="session-terminal__screen">`; `SessionsClient.watch` writing every `bytes`; `terminal.onData((text) => void SessionsClient.type(session.id, text))` character for character; cleanup is exactly `subscription.close()` and `terminal.dispose()` and nothing else. `SessionStreamListener` gains `onRefused` (`Sessions.types.ts:11`) and `client.ts:55-60` tells a refusal from an unreachable backend by `source.readyState === EventSource.CLOSED`, computed before `settle()` mutates it — byte for byte the shape of `plan-events/client.ts:35-41`, which the brief names as the thing to copy. Copy: `Esta sesión ya no existe` for the refusal, `No se puede leer esta sesión` for the rest; `aria-label` is `Terminal de la sesión`; `"@xterm/xterm": "^6.0.0"` is in `dependencies` with a matching lockfile entry, and `css/xterm.css` is imported. The amended Contract no longer exports `TERMINAL_COLUMNS`/`TERMINAL_ROWS` and the diff correctly keeps `COLUMNS`/`ROWS` private. On the flagged judgment call — collapsing `onFailure` and `onUnreachable` into one `unreadable` state — the brief itself prescribes it ("`No se puede leer esta sesión` for the rest"), and nothing is lost that exists: `backend/src/infrastructure/session-stream-route.ts` never writes a data-carrying `error` frame (only `plan-events-route.ts` has `failureFrameFor`), so `onFailure` has no producer on this stream and its `code`/`detail` are never populated. The distinction a person in the cabin actually needs — 'this session is gone' versus 'the backend will come back' — is the one the diff preserves.

Rows the diff bears on: P-5 (`@xterm/xterm ^6.0.0`, doubled with `vi.mock` because jsdom cannot measure a terminal, and 'what the test owes is that the bytes reached it') — implemented as written, and it is also the row that closes the question of how far the double has to go. P-8 (Spanish product copy, English everything else) — banner copy and `aria-label` in Spanish, every identifier, type and test name in English. P-3 (the page never opens or kills a session) — the component only watches and types; no `POST /sessions`, no delete, no command. P-2 (a frame carries bytes and nothing else) — `onBytes` reads `bytes` and no `kind` field is introduced. P-9 (`session-not-live`) — not reopened: the browser cannot read a 400 body through `EventSource`, and the page maps the closed connection to 'gone' rather than inventing a second code. D-21 (no phase of the cabin hides or disables the conversation's input) — the input stays wired even when a banner shows, since the banner is rendered beside the screen, not instead of it. No row is implemented with a different value.

Exemplars: `plan-events/client.ts` is reproduced exactly in `client.ts`'s new refusal branch, and `ImplementProgress.tsx` is matched role for role — a `<section>` with an `aria-label`, `Banner type="error" role="alert" title=…`, a `.css` beside it and an `index.ts` re-exporting the component and its props type in the same two lines as `implement-progress/index.ts`. `frontend/README.md`: no semicolons, named exports, absolute imports from `src/`, one component per file, BEM under `.session-terminal`, Spanish labels — all held; the automated yardstick (`frontend/__tests__/yardstick.test.ts`) is part of the green run. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — `type SessionStreamState = 'streaming' | 'gone' | 'unreadable'` is a closed union and the absent-failure state is a member of it rather than an optional, exactly as the document asks; the JSX dispatch has no catch-all branch; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: nothing in the diff returns a map, `LiveSession` and `SessionStreamSubscription` are declared types and the component returns JSX; (3) two fields that have to agree / sentinel — no subject: one `useState` holds the whole state with no flag beside it, and `const refused = source.readyState === EventSource.CLOSED` is a local derived from the platform's own enum, not a stored second field; (4) an error named for where it happens — no subject in production code; the only `throw` in the diff is the test helper's `'no terminal was created'`, which names what happened. `conventions/boundaries.md`: the one cast in the diff (`Terminal as unknown as { instances }`) is a test reaching into its own double, not a boundary cast. Two tensions declared rather than reported: (a) `conventions/style.md`'s 'no free function at module level' cannot be satisfied by a React 19 function component — hooks do not exist on a class, and the Contract block prescribes `useEffect`/`useState` — so the component's own shape is the only one the implementer could have written; (b) `conventions/testing.md` asks that the objects a test needs come from a mother, and `SESSION = { id: 'a1', name: 'zsh' }` duplicates `SessionsMother`'s constants, but `__scenarios__/SessionsMother.ts` answers wire bodies rather than `LiveSession` objects and is not in this task's `**Files:**`, so using it would have required a path the mechanical scope check refuses. Both are the plan's, not the diff's. Two `low` findings recorded below.

The diff touches one pre-existing test file, `frontend/src/app/sessions/client.test.ts`, and every line it writes there is a `+`: the new `it('a connection the browser closed for good is a refusal')` and a single `onRefused: () => undefined,` added to the listener literal of the existing 'the bytes of a frame reach the listener', which the widened `SessionStreamListener` type requires. No assertion, case or test is removed, relaxed or rewritten. The only `-` lines in the whole diff are in the plan document, which is prose and not a test.

The promised behaviour lives in production code. `SessionTerminal.tsx` is the real component under test; what is doubled is the third-party emulator, which P-5 closes as a decision ('jsdom cannot measure a terminal'), and every assertion is on something production code did: `lastTerminal().written` is the payload the production `onBytes` handed the library, `posting` is the real global `fetch` receiving the literal `/sessions/a1/input` request that `SessionsClient.type` built, `FakeEventSource.last().closes` is the real `source.close()` the production cleanup triggered, and the two banner assertions read DOM text that only the component's state machine can put there. Revert any of those production lines and the corresponding test dies — which is what the implementer's declared mutation of the two forwardings, the `onRefused` branch and the cleanup `dispose()` confirms. No hard-coded expected value stands in for a computation, and no behaviour exists only in the fixture. What the double does hide is `terminal.open(screen)`, reported as a `low` under `patrones` rather than here, because the line exists and is correct — it is unwatched, not absent.

Inside the declared files, every line traces to a sentence of the task. The `package-lock.json` hunk is what `npm --prefix frontend install` produces — the `@xterm/xterm` entry the brief orders, plus the root `"license": "MIT"` npm copies from a `package.json` that already declared it — not a hand edit. `setState('streaming')` at the head of the effect is the one line not spelled out in the Contract, and it is what makes the prescribed key on `session.id` correct: without it a banner from the previous session would survive the switch. `index.ts` re-exports the props type, which is verbatim the shape of the `implement-progress/index.ts` the plan names. Nothing in `### Out of scope` is touched: the eight endpoints are untouched, no `kind` field is added to the frame, no resize and no endpoint that opens or kills a session appears (no fit addon, fixed 80x24). The plan hunk is an AMENDMENT and I read it line by line: it widens this task's `**Files:**` by three paths (`Sessions.types.ts`, `client.ts`, `client.test.ts`) rather than narrowing it, replaces the weak control `test "$(grep -c 'xterm' frontend/package.json)" -eq 1` with a real suite run of `client.test.ts`, and swaps `it('a refused stream shows the code the backend answered')` — unimplementable, since a browser cannot read a 400 body through `EventSource` — for a banner test plus a new client-level test, so the test set gets stronger, not weaker. The operator declared this hunk as their own edit; it is justified on its own terms either way.

Five new tests in `SessionTerminal.test.tsx` and one in `client.test.ts`. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no randomness, no sleep, no network and no path — `EventSource` and `fetch` are both stubbed and `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` runs after each. Isolated: `FakeEventSource.install()` resets `opened` in `beforeEach`, `vitest`'s `globals: true` gives `@testing-library/react` its automatic unmount between tests, and although `MockTerminal.instances` is never cleared, `lastTerminal()` reads `.at(-1)` and every test renders its own component first, so no test depends on the order of the others or on state another test left. Verifies real behaviour: each assertion is on what the production code did — the bytes it wrote, the request it posted, the source it closed, the text it rendered — and every one of them fails if the production line behind it is reverted. Beyond the three, I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` and its `testing-anti-patterns.md`: the `vi.mock('@xterm/xterm')` double is not Anti-Pattern 1 (nothing asserts on the mock's existence; the assertions are on what the component passed it), not Anti-Pattern 3 (the doubled side effect — drawing — is not what any test depends on), and its four members are exactly the four the production code calls, so it is not an incomplete mock of a payload; the setup is roughly 28 of 101 lines, under the 'mock setup is >50% of test' red flag. Nothing here rises to a finding.

findings.what: `terminal.open(screen)` is the single line that puts anything on screen, and no test watches it: the double's `open() {}` records nothing, so deleting the call leaves all five tests green and the cabin showing an empty box. The declared mutation sweep covers four lines — the two forwardings, the `onRefused` branch and the cleanup `dispose()` — and this is not among them; neither is the `{ cols: COLUMNS, rows: ROWS }` argument nor the `aria-label="Terminal de la sesión"` the brief pins. The double supports the fix cheaply (record the parent in `open` and assert it is the ref'd screen). Kept at `low` rather than blocking because P-5 already closed what the test owes here — 'what the test owes is that the bytes reached it' — and because a blank terminal is exactly what the human `visual` gate on this task would catch.
findings.evidence: conventions/testing.md: "After each round, mutate the production code one change at a time, run the whole suite, and hunt the mutations that leave it green: each one is a line no test is watching."

findings.what: `lastTerminal` is a helper at module level in a file created by this diff, so it cannot claim the declared-debt exemption a module that was already there gets. `conventions/style.md` wants every function hanging off a type and `conventions/testing.md` says test helpers hang off their test type; a static on a namespace class beside the double would be the realizable form here. Kept at `low`: every frontend test file in the tree writes its helpers this way, including `client.test.ts`'s `answering` and the other files §3 names as exemplars, so this is repository-wide debt rather than a defect this diff introduced, and with `describe`/`it` there is no test type to hang it off other than a namespace invented for the purpose. The component function itself is excluded from this finding — React hooks make a class impossible, and the Contract block prescribes `useEffect`.
findings.evidence: conventions/testing.md: "Test helpers hang off their test type, like any other function." — and conventions/style.md: "No free function at module level: every function hangs off a type."
